content_voiceover: These are the week ninety six MMR results from ASC4FIRST, updating the primary week forty eight readout. Look at the overall comparison first: asciminib versus all investigator selected TKIs. At week forty eight, sixty seven point seven percent of asciminib patients achieved major molecular response versus forty nine percent on investigator selected TKIs, an eighteen point nine percent difference that was statistically significant. By week ninety six, that gap held, seventy four point one versus fifty two percent, a twenty two point four percent difference, meeting the key secondary endpoint. In the imatinib specific stratum, the difference was even larger, sixty nine point three versus forty point two percent at week forty eight, widening slightly to seventy six point two versus forty seven point one percent at week ninety six. Interestingly, in the second generation TKI stratum, the treatment difference actually grew from week forty eight to week ninety six, sixty six versus fifty seven point eight percent, up to seventy two versus fifty six point nine percent. The overall message: asciminib's molecular response advantage is durable and, in some subgroups, increases over time.
keypoints: Asciminib maintained superior MMR versus all investigator selected TKIs at week 96
Advantage versus imatinib specifically was the largest, about thirty percentage points
Treatment difference versus 2G TKIs increased between week 48 and week 96
Both primary and key secondary endpoints were met with durable benefit
keypoint_voiceover: The key takeaway is durability. Asciminib's molecular response advantage did not fade by week ninety six, it held or even widened across all three comparisons, overall, versus imatinib, and versus second generation TKIs. This strengthens the case for asciminib as a credible first line option, not just an early responder.
